svg.title: Figure 8-1. FTTI scenes: the lateral safety goals (WP-C-04 §8)
svg.desc: One card per safety goal, the lateral safety goals: SG-01 If the panda's own processor faults, steering must stop within 0.5 s; SG-02 If steering is lost, the driver must be warned within 1 s; SG-05 When the driver steers against it, the torque must back off within 0.2 s.
svg.text: Figure 8-1. FTTI scenes: the lateral safety goals

Each card: the §8 FTTI budget against today; what the safety mechanism must prevent (schematic, loops every 6 s); the timeline from fault to safe state; what it must do and does today; who carries the FSRs and how many are met.
Goals, FSRs, trace, budgets and implementation status from WP-C-04 §3, §5, §8 and §9. The scenes and the times shown for today are schematic, not measurements.

g.title: SG-01: If the panda's own processor faults, steering must stop within 0.5 s
g.text: SG-01 · ASIL C ⚠ · SAFE STATE: TORQUE 0, REQUEST CLEARED
If the panda's own processor faults,
H-01 unintended steering · FTTI ≤ 0.5 s · 14 FSRs serve it
WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST PREVENT · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Without it: a stuck command steers on
FAULT TO SAFE STATE · NEEDED AGAINST TODAY
WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST DO
Detect its own execution faults (hang, clock,
memory) and go silent, with the relay released,
The baseline had no hardware watchdog (GAP-07). A 90 ms
watchdog is in all builds since panda 3859fa8 and counts once
WHO CARRIES THE 14 FSRs SERVING SG-01 (§9, §5 ALLOC)

g.title: SG-02: If steering is lost, the driver must be warned within 1 s
g.text: SG-02 · ASIL C · SAFE STATE: WARNING, TORQUE RAMP-DOWN
If steering is lost, the driver must
H-02 silent loss of steering · FTTI ≤ 1 s to warning · 16 FSRs serve it
FTTI BUDGET (§8) · SG-02, SG-06 (LOSS WITHOUT WARNING)
warns at once, actuates on stale inputs ≈ 3.5 s
WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST PREVENT · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Lateral control lost at the curve
Soft disable: alert, but stale actuation
≈ 0.7 s to 0.6 m drift in this curve
FAULT TO SAFE STATE · NEEDED AGAINST TODAY
WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST DO
Detect a loss of lateral control within 0.5 s, warn
within 1 s, and stop acting on inputs it no longer
The soft disable warns at once but keeps actuating on stale
inputs for up to about 3.5 s (GAP-16). In the ODD's tightest
curve 0.7 s already gives 0.6 m of drift (WP-S-04 §3.2).
WHO CARRIES THE 16 FSRs SERVING SG-02 (§9, §5 ALLOC)

g.title: SG-05: When the driver steers against it, the torque must back off within 0.2 s
g.text: SG-05 · ASIL B ⚠ · SAFE STATE: DISENGAGED
When the driver steers against it, the
torque must back off within 0.2 s
H-05 cannot override · FTTI ≤ 0.2 s · 12 FSRs serve it
not in the envelope: never backs off
WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST PREVENT · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
The envelope has no override check
FAULT TO SAFE STATE · NEEDED AGAINST TODAY

svg.text: no driver-torque check in the envelope

g.text: WHAT THE SAFETY MECHANISM MUST DO
Detect the driver's steering override, ramp the
torque toward zero for as long as it lasts, and show
Brake and cancel are in the envelope; steering override is
not, so the torque keeps coming (GAP-02). The back-off is
WHO CARRIES THE 12 FSRs SERVING SG-05 (§9, §5 ALLOC)
